claims.value: 14 .baf files, one per run, each on a heavy and a light row
claims.evidence: The 14 RAW-category files of the deposit are Bruker analysis.baf files renamed to the run name. Each mgf header names its source "...\<run>.d\analysis.baf"; each mzid names its mgf and its .dat. Chain: MKL-1: MKL1_RA1_01_8251/125/126 (mzid MKL_1_3/1/2, dat F039768/53/54, mgf ...013/010/011); MKL-2: MKL2_RA1_01_8254/134/135 (MKL_2_3/1/2; F039770/69/57; ...017/015/016); PeTa: Peta_RA1_01_8261/158/159 (Peta_3/1/2; F039772/56/58; ...022/019/020); WaGa: Waga_RA1_01_8271/122/123 (Waga_8271/122/123; F039777/59/60; ...028/025/026); MCC13: MCC13_RA1_01_8265/8266 (MCC13_2/1; F039765/66; ...008/009). Assay name = file name without .baf. Search outputs, peak lists and PRIDE-generated files are not data runs.

claims.location: comment[label] + characteristics[cell line] + factor value[cell line] rows 1-28
claims.value: SILAC heavy = the MCC cell line named in the run file; SILAC light = HaCaT
claims.evidence: Paper Methods: "For SILAC labelling cells were grown in SILAC Media supplemented either with 13C6 l-Lysine-2HCl (heavy) and l-Arginine-HCl (light) or with l-Lysine-2HCl (light)"; Fig. 1 legend: "MCC cells were cultured in medium supplemented with 13C6 l-Lysine-2HCl (heavy) and HaCaT cells were cultured in medium supplemented with l-Lysine-2HCl (light)"; Results: "Proteins detected in MCC cells were compared to the reference cell line HaCaT"; ratios reported as H/L MCC vs HaCaT. Cell line per run from the run-file prefix (MKL1, MKL2, Peta, Waga, MCC13), which matches the paper's line names. Data check (orientation.txt, weak because only 107-390 PSMs pass per mzid): heavy-only search (Mascot MODS fixed Label:13C(6) (K)) identifies 13C6-Lys peptides of the neuroendocrine MCC marker chromogranin A in MKL-1 (MKL_1_2), MKL-2 (MKL_2_1) and WaGa (Waga_122/123/8271) runs, of TBB3 in MKL-2 and ENO2 in MCC13; the keratinocyte marker KRT5 is never seen in MKL-1/MKL-2/PeTa/WaGa runs and in MCC13 runs mostly by K-free (label-agnostic) peptides (1 heavy vs 13 K-free PSMs). Consistent with heavy = MCC, light = HaCaT. No conflicting statement found.

One SILAC mixture per MCC line (paper: "equimolar amounts of proteins, 1 µg total proteins, from control and the MCC cells were mixed and submitted for tryptic digestion"; "aliquots of 20 µl were prepared"). The HaCaT light channel of each mixture gets its own source name per mixture (reference precedent PXD005854/PXD009766), so the row coordinate stays unique.

Paper: "All samples were analysed as technical triplicates". Runs per line: MKL-1, MKL-2, PeTa, WaGa 3 each; MCC13 only 2 deposited. Numbering: the run stored under folder D:\Data\muw\hno\150531silac (4-digit run number) = 1, then the D:\Data\muw\hno_silac\160817 runs in ascending run number = 2, 3 (mgf headers). Both MCC13 runs are in the 150531 folder (8265 = 1, 8266 = 2).

Paper: "Three biological replicates were cultured per each cell line, and these were merged into one sample upon cell lysis for further treatment." Each cell line is therefore one (pooled) sample -> biological replicate 1 within each factor-value (cell line) group, pooled sample = pooled. For HaCaT this assumes the same statement covers the reference line (the paragraph lists HaCaT among the cell lines cultured); the HaCaT rows of the five mixtures share biological replicate 1 because nothing indicates separate HaCaT cultures per mixture.

claims.value: Carbamidomethyl C fixed; Oxidation M variable; Acetyl K variable; Label:13C(6) K (UNIMOD:188) MT=Variable
claims.evidence: All 14 .dat files: MODS=Carbamidomethyl (C),Label:13C(6) (K); IT_MODS=Acetyl (K),Oxidation (M) (masses section FixedMod2=6.020129 Label:13C(6) (K), delta1=42.010565 Acetyl (K)). The Mascot identification search treated Label:13C(6) K as FIXED (heavy-only identification, light partner quantified by WARP-LC); the SDRF writes MT=Variable per campaign rule 11 because the label is present only on the heavy channel. UNIMOD:188 = Label:13C(6), +6.020 Da, matches the paper's 13C6-lysine. Arginine was light in both channels, so no Arg label.
No fractionation: each tryptic aliquot injected directly (one .baf per injection).

limitations: Partial scope relative to the paper: the paper analysed six MCC lines incl. BroLi, but no BroLi run is deposited (14 .baf: MKL-1 x3, MKL-2 x3, PeTa x3, WaGa x3, MCC13 x2). MCC13 has 2 instead of 3 technical replicates. Nothing deposited was left out, so nothing is BLOCKED.

Channel-map data check is weak: the deposited mzid files contain only 107-390 passing PSMs per run and WARP-LC H/L ratios are not deposited (Tables S1/S2 list proteins without ratios; mzTab are PRIDE-generated identification files). The map rests on the explicit paper statement (Methods + Fig. 1 legend), supported by heavy 13C6-Lys chromogranin A/TBB3/ENO2 PSMs in MCC runs.

Runs of each line come from two acquisition folders (150531silac and 160817, mgf headers), i.e. probably acquired about 15 months apart. Whether the 2015 and 2016 injections are from the same SILAC mixture/aliquot series or a re-prepared mixture is not stated; they are annotated as technical replicates as the paper describes ("technical triplicates").

Whether one HaCaT light lysate served all five mixtures, and whether the "three biological replicates merged" statement covers HaCaT, is not explicit; HaCaT rows all carry biological replicate 1 and pooled.

Search: Mascot searched heavy-only (Label:13C(6) K fixed); recorded as MT=Variable per campaign rule 11. ProteinScape 3.1.5 / Mascot 2.6 / WARP-LC 1.3 were used; WARP-LC quantitation settings are not deposited.
comment[data file] lists the deposited Bruker analysis.baf files (renamed to the run name), not .d directories, because that is what PRIDE holds.
Collision energy (15-35 eV ramp) not encoded; MS1 range not encoded (the mgf 400-2200 values are DataAnalysis export settings, not acquisition settings).
sdrf-tools check flags the MCC cell line names as not found in CLO/BTO/EFO; they are real Cellosaurus entries without an ontology class (see validation.txt).
